newsitem.title: USA: JC Penney focus for US corporate debt, junk mixed.
newsitem.headline: JC Penney focus for US corporate debt, junk mixed.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were firm in the face of $2.5 billion in new paper from J.C. Penney Co on Wednesday, traders said.
High-yield issues were mixed in quiet activity, meanwhile, with better buying spotted in some telecom names. Also, Hills Stores Inc gained on talk it may be a takeover target.

J.C. Penney's issue demanded and received most focus as it was repeatedly restructured and increased in size before the formal pricing hit in mid-afternoon. Shorter-tranches received the best demand, prompting the company to add a new $325 million tranche just prior to pricing.
One money manager, who declined to buy the deal because of "spreads are still too tight," conceded the deal was oversubscribed and "pretty fair within the confines of the corporate market."

The deal, being one of few investment grades offered this week, pressured spreads elsewhere minimally, dealers said. On the contrary, the positive reception for the mega-issue may have shored up market tone following the recent yield back-up.
But most players said the degree of success would be best left to Thursday's secondary market. Possible widening could be seen in the 10-year tranche, one trader said.

It was priced in six tranches with bullet spreads ranging from 40 basis points over Treasuries for in three years to 85 basis points in 20-years; 120 basis points for 30-year non-call 10s; and 50 basis points for 40 year debt with an eight year put option.
Credit Suisse First Boston was lead manager.

Turning to high-yielders, traders reported mostly news driven trading with the exception of a general firmness for the telecom related issues. But buyers were without conviction in the market, they added, and activity was mostly quiet.
Globalstar traded as high as 98-3/4, one trader said. Also, Optel Inc's debt firmed to a 91 bid after its slide to the high 80s last week.

Hills Stores Co debt rose two to three points to 90-1/4 bid, 90-3/4 offer on market talk that it may be a target for retailer ShopKo Inc. Following the breakdown of ShopKo's proposed merger with Phar-Mor Inc, company executives said they would develop a new corporate plan that may focus on the general merchandise business.

Elsewhere, Playtex Family Products nine percent debt dropped one point to 97-1/2 bid, 98-1/4 offer after Proctor & Gamble Co said it would buy Tambrands Inc and its Tampax tampon brand for $1.85 billion.

A big seller of Reeves Industries Inc's 11 percent debt knocked the price down 10 points to 79-1/2. The same was seen in Stuart Entertainment debt -- the 12-1/2s fell four points to 82 from 86 bid, 90 offer.
